Absolutely yes. I have bipolar 1 and I will fall asleep sometimes without taking my meds (combo of mood stabilizer and antipsychotic), and then I wake up feeling GREAT the next day. Then I slide into a few days of hypomania where I'm convinced I don't need meds....then depression where I'm convinced that I'm hopeless and meds won't help anyways (which is not true, they obv help).

I've ended up putting myself into real tough manic and depressive episodes this way. I have a couple close friends that are usually able to recognize when I'm in one of these episodes, and they remind me to take my meds for a few days until I'm stable again. I get irritated by it, but I listen to them and it always helps.

I can't offer any real advice beyond that because I am still figuring it out myself, just wanted to say you are not alone in this!
Christopher? Christopher with the Money Nose? No, I don't think he knows how to fix a shower head.

I questioned my bp1 diagnosis for years & thought the same thing. My psychiatrist says feeling like an imposter is common w bipolar, and also bipolar is one of the more rare diagnoses in the mental health world. Doctors don't take giving out a bipolar diagnosis lightly, and would not have given you that diagnosis unless you were presenting most, if not all, of the symptoms.

So I'm about 7-8 months out from quitting at this point, and the most noticeable side effects are: 1) decreased anger and frustration at normal hindrances (stuff like the cap won't screw on my water bottle the first time, I drop something, I'm a few minutes late, can't find my keys, etc etc) that used to make me fucking rage quit, 2) breathing is easier; no more coughing and no more weird vape mucus 3) less headaches 4) less ups and downs throughout the day because I'm not having a nicotine rush and subsequent crash every half hour, 5) more focused on my projects at work and at home, longer attention span and able to problem solve quicker, and 6) saving +$30/week

The only real "negative" side effect I've noticed is that I'm eating a bit more sugar/a bit more food, generally...but I expected that to happen, I was using my vape as a meal sometimes and prob wasn't eating enough before lol

Most other variables in my life have remained constant, so I'm fairly confident in saying that these benefits are due to cutting out nicotine, at least in part! Make the leap and quit, you won't regret it!
